title: I'm entering my own agent. Early access to an AI trading competitions arena.
author: orid7
selftext:
This is going to be interesting.   
  
AI agents trading the same live market head to head, every fill priced by the platform , one public leaderboard, prizes up to $20,000. Zero risk. free to enter.

Full disclosure, I'm one of the builders, so take my hype with a grain of salt.   
But I'm putting my own trading agent in the competitions.

Early sign-ups close Oct 10: [https://www.letitrade.com/](https://letitrade.com/?utm_source=reddit&utm_content=ai_trading)  
  
let me know if you're in. And tell me what would stop you from entering yours.

comments.author: profittoinvest
comments.body:
This looks interesting. Before entering, one thing would matter a lot to us: does the trading agent remain fully on our infrastructure and only communicate with your arena through an API, or do participants have to upload their strategy/agent code to your platform?

We already run a live-tested crypto bot, but protecting the strategy IP would be a requirement for us.

replies.author: orid7
replies.body: Yes, it stays on your infrastructure. Your agent only talks to the arena through the API (orders in, fills back), you never upload code or prompts. Crypto is one of the first markets we're opening. How long does your bot usually hold a trade?

replies.author: profittoinvest
replies.body:
Our holding times can be quite long.

In the current setup, the average trade duration is around 4–5 days, but some positions can stay open much longer, especially when the market moves against the initial entry and later mean-reverts.

We use relatively deep stops, so the bot is designed to give positions room rather than force quick exits.

That also means we manage risk at the portfolio level, because several older positions can accumulate at the same time.

So it’s definitely more of a multi-day / swing-style system than a fast intraday bot.  
If your arena supports positions being held for days rather than minutes or hours, it could actually be a good fit for us.

Are you aiming to build a platform along the lines of Cornix and 3Commas?

replies.author: orid7
replies.body: The arena takes orders through its own API, but forwarding the same signals to a webhook is usually a small step. And we're opening several competition types (different markets, intraday and swing), so I'm sure a multi-day bot like yours will find its edge.

comments.author: tradematesHQ
comments.body: Keeping the agent on your own infra is the only sane setup, uploading strategy code to an arena is basically handing over your edge. Multi-day holds with deep stops is a rough fit for a leaderboard that rewards fast fills.

replies.author: orid7
replies.body: Totally, that's why it won't be one board for everyone. Separate leagues for intraday and swing, longer windows for swing, and ranking on risk-adjusted return. Your bot stays on your infra either way
